title: AI SDK v6 UIMessageStream Frame
description: Canonical schema for each `data: ...` payload streamed over SSE by createDeepAgentsHandler and the open-swe SSE proxy. The full body is a sequence of these frames separated by `\n\n`, with optional `: <comment>` keepalive lines per the SSE spec. Every `data-*` entry carries `x-emitted-by`, naming WHICH RUNG emits it: a rung id (the frame is gone from a fork ejected below that rung), "core" (emitted by the transport core, survives every eject), or null (nothing in this repository emits it — its absence from a stream is expected, not a bug). This is an annotation, not a constraint: it tells a reader whether a frame is missing because their fork cannot produce it. It is checked against rungs.json in CI, and `pnpm eject` PRUNES every frame whose x-emitted-by names a dropped rung, so a fork's copy declares only what that fork can speak. #62 relied on the annotation alone, reasoning a reader could cross-reference rungs.json; that keeps the file readable but leaves it wrong as a MACHINE artifact, since a consumer validating against a rung-1 fork's copy would accept data-plan frames that fork can never emit. Frames whose x-emitted-by is "core" or null are never pruned — null marks the deliberate orphans of #50, which a prune-by-missing-producer rule would have deleted. See issues #50 and #59.

oneOf.title: data-task
oneOf.description: DEPRECATED, SUPERSEDED BY `data-todo` (issues #50, #59). Nothing in this repository emits this frame, and nothing will: `data-task` describes a SINGLE task with a status, while `data-todo` carries the whole list and is really emitted by `write_todos`. The single-task form has no tool whose output it uniquely represents, so a producer would have to be invented to justify the contract — which is the same defect as a contract with no producer, facing the other way. It is NOT deleted: it remains published and remains registered in @deepagents-nextjs/react, because removing it would silently narrow a schema consumers may already build against. Use `data-todo` for new work. A consumer's own backend may still emit this shape, and it will still parse.

oneOf.title: data-approval
oneOf.description: OPEN SWE PLAN-MODE GATE, emitted by packages/server/src/adapters/openSweEnrich.ts when the agent calls `enter_plan_mode` and is waiting for a human to approve or reject the plan. Rung-4-owned: a fork ejected below rung 4 can never emit this frame. NOT to be confused with `data-approval-required`, the generic tool-level gate emitted by core. This tag was emitted and consumed for some time while being absent from this schema (issue #59), so a consumer validating strictly against an older copy of this file would have rejected a frame the product really sends.

oneOf.title: data-approval-pause
oneOf.description: UPSTREAM APPROVAL GATE, emitted by packages/server/src/adapters/langchain.ts when a LangChain HITL interrupt withholds a tool call. THE CALL HAS NOT RUN. That is what distinguishes it from `data-approval-required`, which core's proxy transform raises AFTER the backend already executed the tool — that one withholds the report, not the effect. The two must never share an affordance: a cell is either genuinely gated and shows the pause card, or ungated and shows no approval control at all. `core`, not a rung, since #332 armed a second rung and the conversion moved to the shared adapters/approval-pause.ts. The attribution follows the PRODUCER, and that producer is now claimed by no rung -- sse-frame-rung-attribution.test.ts derives it from the source and says so. It was `langchain` while the langchain adapter built the part itself. Naming a rung again would be wrong in both directions: scripts/eject.mjs prunes a frame when its attributed rung is dropped, so `langgraph` would delete it from a rung-1 fork that still emits it, and `langchain` now claims a rung for a file that rung does not own. Which rungs TRIGGER the pause varies by fork; which file emits it does not. The `data` carries upstream's interrupt VERBATIM, snake_case keys included — `action_requests` paired BY INDEX with `review_configs`, whose `allowed_decisions` is the client's only source for which controls to offer. This frame was emitted and consumed for some time while absent from this schema and from SCHEMA_MAP, so it was parsed by nothing and dropped silently before any component could see it (#448).

oneOf.title: data-approval-required
oneOf.description: GENERIC TOOL-LEVEL APPROVAL GATE, emitted by core (packages/server/src/approval-gating.ts) AND by rung 5's `request_human_help` gate (packages/server/src/adapters/sdaEnrich.ts). Survives every eject: core is a producer, and core is below every rung, so no rung outranks it here. NOT to be confused with `data-approval`, which is open-swe's plan-mode gate and is rung-4-owned. The two names are close enough that they have already been substituted for one another once (issue #59); check `x-emitted-by` before assuming which one you are looking at. This description named only the core emitter until rung 5 added the second (#12) — a reader grepping for producers would have found two and the doc mentioned one.

oneOf.title: data-agents-md
oneOf.description: DECLARED, NO PRODUCER (issue #50). Nothing in this repository emits this frame. The only code that constructs it is test fixtures, so the renderer tests for it prove that a card renders a well-formed part — not that the part is ever produced. It stays in this schema deliberately: it is a published contract a consumer may already build against, and removing it would silently narrow the schema. Its absence from a live stream is EXPECTED and is not a bug. A producer is tracked as follow-up work.

oneOf.title: data-testing
oneOf.description: TESTING GRAPH STATUS AND RUNS, emitted by packages/server/src/adapters/sdaEnrich.ts from rung 5's `set_testing_status` and `playwright` tools. Rung-5-owned: a fork ejected below rung 5 can never emit this frame. Discriminated on `kind` — "status" is a state transition, "run" is a Playwright invocation. It exists because no existing part can carry it: data-todo's vocabulary is pending|in-progress|done, and "the tests ran and FAILED" versus "testing was SKIPPED because only docs changed" is neither, yet that distinction is the Testing graph's entire output. A seventh status, "unknown", is emitted when a model sends a value outside the tool's enum; it is registered deliberately, because @deepagents-nextjs/react's converter is fail-open and a status the schema forgets is a frame the user never sees.

_xKindNote: x-kind — WHAT KIND OF PAYLOAD THIS IS (#50, ruled).
demonstrated  this repo emits it, mounts it, and a user can watch it fire.
contract      this repo publishes the schema and the card so a CONSUMER'S backend can
fill it. NO PRODUCER HERE, BY DESIGN.
The repo is permanently both a publishable library and a reference implementation, so
'declared with no producer' is two different facts wearing one word: a defect for the nine
the repo demonstrates, and the intended shape for the two it only publishes. Asserting one
rule over both would either excuse a real gap or demand a producer that must not exist.
BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE ASSERTED in scripts/payload-triangulation.mjs, per #424's precedent:
demonstrated => HAS a producer here AND is mounted
contract     => is mounted AND has NO producer here
The second is the one that would otherwise be silent: if someone later adds a data-task
emitter, the check DEMANDS RECLASSIFICATION rather than going quietly green. A rule that
can only fail toward today's worry is a rename, not a control.
Do not 'fix' a contract part by manufacturing a producer. rungs.json records both as
exercised only by hand-crafted SSE in tests; promoting a fixture into the product would
teach a forker that a framework emits something no framework emits.
